source: Arianespace user-manual reference points and NASA SLS design-study curves

vehicles.ground_rules: Ariane 6 User's Manual, Issue 2 Revision 0 (February 2021), section 2.4.5, printed p.2-11. V-infinity=2.5 km/s, hence C3=6.25; free declination. Section 2.2 defines payload mass including the adapter/dispenser and any carrying structure. Disposal strategy may require mission-specific optimization. This is one published point, not a full curve or a rating for later booster upgrades. No extrapolation.

vehicles.source_label: NASA design curve · 2020 · approximate graph readings
vehicles.ground_rules: NASA's Space Launch System: Capabilities for Ultra-High C3 Missions (2020), Figure 3. Black SLS Block 1 cargo curve, 5 m fairing; usable payload system mass, not spacecraft dry mass. Approximate digitized readings rounded to 100 kg; graph reading and linear interpolation add uncertainty, not a quantified confidence interval. Historical design prediction, not a current provider commitment. Retained samples cover C3 0-130 only; no extrapolation.

vehicles.source_label: NASA concept curve · 2020 · approximate graph readings
vehicles.ground_rules: NASA's Space Launch System: Capabilities for Ultra-High C3 Missions (2020), Figure 6, solid red SLS Block 2 with an additional Centaur third stage, departure declination 28.5 degrees. This is an unflown study configuration, not the baseline SLS or a currently bookable vehicle. Study assumes mean vehicle mass, nominal liquid engines, low-performance booster and an 8.4 m by 19.1 m fairing; the paper removes the manager's reserve. Usable payload system mass. Approximate graph readings rounded to 100 kg; no quantified performance confidence interval. Retained C3 coverage 60-280 only; no extrapolation.
